body.statement: If the menu is specialized to \(M=2\), then \(d=1\), \(L(r)=L_{\sqrt{\Sigma(r)}}(\mathcal H)\), and the exact scale identity is \(L_{\sigma}(\mathcal H)=\sigma L_1(\mathcal H/\sigma)\). If \(0<\sigma_1\le\sigma_2\), then \(N(h,\sigma_1^2)\) Blackwell dominates \(N(h,\sigma_2^2)\) by addition of independent Gaussian noise, so \(L_{\sigma_1}(\mathcal H)\le L_{\sigma_2}(\mathcal H)\). Therefore every design minimizing the single contrast variance is regret-optimal; no converse or strict monotonicity is asserted without an additional condition on \(\mathcal H\).
body.justification: The binary reduction is the required sanity check and isolates why three overlapping policies are the first nontrivial case.
body.gap: Binary Gaussian treatment-choice and Neyman allocation results are known; this proposition verifies exact compatibility rather than claiming novelty.
body.consumer: Readers can diagnose whether the new regret criterion changes design only because the action menu creates genuinely multivariate tie geometry.
